questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

i. The first green revolution led to over-exploitation of natural resources.

ii. The second Green Revolution was more focused on Southern India.

iii. The second green revolution ensured in achieving sustainable livelihood security.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: i. and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first green revolution, which occurred in the 1960s and 1970s, led to over-exploitation of natural resources, particularly water and soil nutrients, due to the intensive use of high-yielding variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation.
 
• The second green revolution aimed to address the shortcomings of the first by focusing on sustainable agricultural practices and technologies that would ensure long-term productivity without depleting natural resources.
 
• The second green revolution was not just focused on Southern India, it was more holistic, including various regions to ensure sustainable agricultural development.
 
• i. The first green revolution led to over-exploitation of natural resources. iii. The second green revolution ensured in achieving sustainable livelihood security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that occurred between the 1940s and the late 1960s. It increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• The initiatives resulted in the adoption of new high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• While the Green Revolution significantly increased food production and alleviated hunger in many parts of the world, it also led to environmental degradation and increased inequality among farmers.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture**
 
 
• Sustainable agriculture is the practice of farming using principles of ecology, the study of relationships between organisms and their environment.
 
• This approach includes methods such as crop rotation, reduced use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, conservation tillage, and organic farming to maintain soil health and biodiversity.
 
• The goal is to meet current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
 
 
• **Livelihood Security**
 
 
• Livelihood security refers to securing adequate and sustainable access to income and resources to meet basic needs, including food, water, health, education, housing, and time for community participation and social integration.
 
• Sustainable livelihood security takes into account the long-term capacity to maintain these assets in the face of stresses and shocks.
 
 
 
• **First and Second Green Revolutions**
 
 
• The First Green Revolution focused on increasing agricultural productivity through high-yield variety seeds, chemical inputs, and irrigation.
 
• The Second Green Revolution emphasizes sustainable practices, biotechnology, and integrated pest management to ensure long-term productivity and environmental health.

questions.question: Shifting agriculture is known as ______ in the Western Ghats.

__
 
• **Shifting cultivation, under the names Kumari**, Hakkal, or Punam( local names). It has been an important agricultural system in the Western Ghats.
 
• **Shifting cultivation** is a form of agricultural practice in which farmers clear an area of land by slashing vegetation and burning forests for agricultural purposes.
 
• This practice is also known as slash-and-burn agriculture or slash-and-burn cultivation.
 
• **Jhum or Jhoom cultivation** is also known as shifting cultivation or cultivation or slash and burn cultivation.
 
• **Jhum cultivation** was practised in Central Highland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Shifting Cultivation Process **

 
• Each year farmers choose an area for planting.
 
• They have to remove vegetation that typically covers the land.
 
• They cut most of the trees with the help of axes, which are economically helpful.
 
• In different regions, the cleared area is called Swidden, Ladang, milpa, Chena, and Kaingin.
 
• They cultivate the cleared land only briefly, usually three or fewer seasons.
 
• Farmers leave the old site uncropped for 10 to 25 years.
 
• They will return to the land after 10 to 20 years to cultivate again.

questions.question: In which of the soil conservation methods in the coastal and dry regions, rows of trees are planted to check the wind movement to protect soil cover?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shelter belts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shelter belts are rows of** trees and shrubs planted to protect soil from wind erosion, particularly in coastal and arid regions.**
 
• These tree lines reduce wind **speed across the ground and thereby decrease the wind's ability to lift and carry soil particles away, combating wind erosion effectively.**
 
• Apart from reducing **wind erosion, shelter belts also offer additional benefits like providing habitat for wildlife, sequestering carbon, and enhancing the landscape's aesthetics.**
 
• This method is quite common in **flat, dry regions where wind erosion is a major issue, such as parts of North America, Africa, and Asia.**
 
• Shelter belts can take the form of **single or multiple rows of trees or shrubs,** depending on the severity of the wind erosion problem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulching:**

 
 
• Mulching involves covering the soil surface with a layer of organic or inorganic material **(like straw, leaves, compost, or plastic sheets).**
 
• This technique **retains soil moisture, suppresses weed growth, and can also prevent soil erosion by reducing the impact of raindrops on the soil surface.**
 
 
 
• **Rock Dam:**
 
 
• Rock dams are barriers built across channels, gullies, or small waterways using rocks.
 
• They slow down the flow of water, reduce its erosive power and trap sediments.
 
• **This technique is commonly used in mountainous regions or areas prone to flash floods and gully erosion.**
 
 
 
• **Contour Barriers:**
 
 
• **​**Contour barriers are physical barriers like **stones, vegetation, or soil bunds constructed along the contours of a slope.**
 
• **They slow down water runoff, promote water infiltration, and reduce soil erosion by water.**
 
• This method is typically used on sloping land in both farming and forestry.

questions.question: What was a significant negative environmental impact of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil degradation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution led to the extensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, which resulted in the degradation of soil quality.
 
• Overuse of these chemicals destroyed beneficial soil microorganisms, making the soil less fertile over time.
 
• High-yielding varieties of crops required more water and nutrients, leading to the depletion of soil nutrients and increased soil salinity.
 
• Monocropping practices associated with the Green Revolution reduced the organic matter in the soil, further contributing to soil degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries, starting in the 1960s.
 
• Key components included the development of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of staple crops, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the introduction of modern farming techniques.
 
• The main aim was to achieve food security and reduce hunger by increasing crop yields.
 
 
 
• **Soil Degradation**
 
 
• Soil degradation is the decline in soil quality caused by its improper use, usually for agricultural, industrial, or urban purposes.
 
• It involves the loss of soil's physical, chemical, and biological properties, which affects its ability to sustain plant life and provide ecosystem services.
 
• Factors contributing to soil degradation include erosion, salinization, compaction, loss of soil organic matter, and contamination by toxic substances.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides**
 
 
• Chemical fertilizers are substances that supply essential nutrients to plants in the form of compounds like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
 
• Pesticides are chemicals used to kill or control pests that can damage crops.
 
• Excessive use of these chemicals can lead to environmental issues such as soil degradation, water pollution, and harm to non-target organisms.
 
 
 
• **Monocropping**
 
 
• Monocropping is the agricultural practice of growing the same crop on the same piece of land year after year.
 
• This practice can lead to soil nutrient depletion, increased vulnerability to pests and diseases, and reduced biodiversity.
 
• It often requires higher inputs of fertilizers and pesticides to maintain crop yields, contributing to soil degradation and environmental pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions could harm tea plantations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Temperature above 35°C. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Conditions required for tea plantations:**
 
• Well-distributed rainfall of around **150-300 cm** is considered suitable for successful tea production.
 
• The monthly average maximum temperature range between 28°C and 32°C during April to September.
 
 
• **Hence ****Temperature above 35°C is harmful.**
 
 
 
• As far as soil conditions are concerned, generally, sandy loam to silty loam type of soil with a pH range of 4.5-5.5 is ideal for growing tea.
 
• Tea is a **shade-loving plant** and develops more vigorously when planted along with shady trees.
 
• Soil should possess a minimum of 1% of organic carbon, 1-2% of organic matter, 35ppm of P2O5 and K2O for the successful establishment of tea.
 
• Planting of tea is done either in spring (June-July) after the first few showers of rain or in autumn (October-November) while the soil is still moist and the area has irrigation facilities.

__
 
• The Second Green Revolution aimed at **enhancing productivity** sustainably through modern agricultural practices.
 
• It focused on **diversification** of crops, not just staple cereals, to ensure a balanced growth in agriculture.
 
• The initiative aimed to **integrate technology** and innovation in farming, including the use of biotechnology and precision farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

• It involved the development of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, increased use of fertilizers and irrigation methods, which significantly boosted agricultural production in many developing countries, including India.

• Green Revolution in India : 

 
 
• At independence, about 75 per cent of the country’s population was dependent on agriculture.
 
• Productivity in the agricultural sector was very low because of the use of old technology and the absence of the required infrastructure for the vast majority of farmers.
 
• India’s agriculture vitally depends on the monsoon and if the monsoon fell short the farmers were in trouble unless they had access to irrigation facilities which very few had.
 
• The stagnation in agriculture during colonial rule was permanently broken by the green revolution.
 
• This refers to the large increase in the production of food grains resulting from the use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, **especially for wheat and rice. **
 
• The use of these seeds required the use of fertilizer and pesticide in the correct quantities as well as a regular supply of water; the application of these inputs in correct proportions is vital. 
 
• The farmers who could benefit from HYV seeds required reliable irrigation facilities as well as financial resources to purchase fertilizer and pesticides.
 
• As a result, in the first phase of the green revolution (the approximately mid-1960s up to mid-1970s), the use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent states such as Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Further, the use of HYV seeds primarily benefited the wheat-growing regions only. In the second phase of the green revolution (the mid-1970s to mid-1980s), the HYV technology spread to a larger number of states and benefited more variety of crops.
 
• The spread of green revolution technology-enabled India to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains; we no longer had to be at the mercy of America, or any other nation, for meeting our nation’s food requirements.

__
 
• **Modern agricultural** technology, **Green revolution,** and **Seed-fertiliser-water** technology are all related to **increasing agricultural productivity** and efficiency, while **White revolution** is related to the** increase in milk production** in India.
 
• **Green revolution **refers to the use of **high-yielding varieties** of **crops,** **improved irrigation**, and **modern agricultural techniques** to increase crop productivity.
 
 
• It was introduced in India in the 1960s and led to a **significant increase** in food production.
 
 
 
• **Seed-fertiliser-water technology** is a modern agricultural technique that involves using **high-quality seeds**, **appropriate fertilizers,** and **efficient irrigation methods** to increase crop yields.
 
• **Modern agricultural technology** encompasses a wide range of techniques and methods, including** precision farming, biotechnology, and mechanization**, among others.

• It aimed to increase milk production and make India** self-sufficient** in milk production.
 
• The program was successful in increasing milk production and creating a **cooperative network** of milk producers in India.
 
• It led to the establishment of **Amul, a dairy cooperative** that has become a household name in India.
 
• The success of the White revolution was due to the efforts of **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, who is often referred to as the **father of the White revolution** in India.

• Hydroponics: 

 
 
• It is also known as soil-less culture or water culture.
 
• In 1860, Julius Von Sachs a prominent German botanist first demonstrated this process.
 
• The hydroponics method is used to increase the yield of ornamental flowers, such as snapdragons, roses, etc., and vegetables, such as carrots, radishes, potatoes, tomatoes, lettuce, etc.
 
• Julius Von Sachs demonstrated that plants can grow without soil if plants are provided with a nutrient-rich solution and fulfil their required oxygen demand.
 
• Hydroponics is an innovative method of farming and is widely used for yielding food crops.
 
• This technique is used to know which mineral elements are essential for the growth and development of plants.
 
 
 
• The advantages of the hydroponics technique are the following-
 
 
• The yield of production is high as plants grow faster.
 
• Plants can grow anywhere, rooftops, greenhouses, etc.
 
• Used nutrient solutions and water can be reused or recycled.
 
• Organic food can be cultivated without using fertilizers or pesticides.
 
• It is a pollution-free agricultural method.
 
 
 
• Some disadvantages of this method are in the following-
 
 
• Need a high amount of investment.
 
• Requires various technical knowledge.
 
 
 
• A hydroponic setup requires some components, such as a reservoir, one grow tray, a growing medium, and a nutrient solution.
 
 
• Plants grow faster as compared to that in soil.
